Key contributor · Apple MLX ecosystem

Gökdeniz
Gülmez.

System Engineer at Computacenter · ML Engineer · Researcher. In my day job, I focus on ML engineering and MLOps. In my free time, I contribute to open source and pursue ML research and engineering. I’m a key contributor to Apple’s MLX framework and MLX-LM, bringing a wide range of model architectures and training capabilities to local AI on Apple Silicon. I maintain the MLX-VLM trainer backend and develop the J.O.S.I.E. model family.

01 / About

I bring frontier models
to Apple Silicon.

At Computacenter, I work as a System Engineer focused on ML engineering and MLOps. Outside work, I contribute to open source and pursue ML research and engineering. Across the MLX framework, MLX-LM, MLX Examples and MLX-VLM, that work spans core training primitives, model architecture support, and the trainer backend for vision-language models.

02 / Upstream

I help build the MLX stack.

Across core MLX, MLX-LM, MLX Examples and MLX-VLM, I work on the pieces that make more models trainable and usable on Apple Silicon. The upstream projects credit specific contributions below.

01Core framework · MLX

New training primitives

I added the Muon optimizer and ReLU² activation function to core MLX—foundational capabilities now credited in the framework’s contributor acknowledgements.

See MLX acknowledgements ↗
02Language models · MLX-LM

Architectures at scale

I’ve brought a wide range of model families into MLX-LM, alongside full-weight fine-tuning, Muon, multi-optimizer training and Weights & Biases reporting. DeepSeek-V4.1 support was contributed in a merged upstream pull request.

Read MLX-LM credits ↗
03Vision-language · MLX-VLM

Training backend maintainer

I’m the main maintainer of MLX-VLM’s trainer backend. I rebuilt the training path and added ORPO support, bringing more fine-tuning capability to vision-language models running on Apple Silicon.

Explore MLX-VLM ↗
04Examples · MLX Examples

Workflows people can run

The MLX Examples project credits my work on MiniCPM, Helium, Mamba v1 and OLMoE support, as well as full-fine-tuning support.

Read MLX Examples credits ↗

03 / Research

Researching how
models learn and act.

Preprint · 2026

DynaMoE

A Mixture-of-Experts design with token-dependent expert activation and layer-wise capacity schedules—studying adaptive compute and how expert allocation shapes learning.

Read the paper ↗
Preprint · 2025

Gabliteration

An adaptive, multi-directional weight-modification method for changing selected model behaviors while trying to preserve performance on unrelated tasks.

Read the paper ↗
Preference optimization · ongoing

Directional Latent Preference Optimization

DLPO explores preference learning with latent-space regularization, aligning output preferences with changes in a model’s internal representations.

Project notes ↗

04 / Model family

J.O.S.I.E. —
models with character.

My open model family · Hugging Face

Reasoning-first models, built locally.

J.O.S.I.E. is a continuing model family exploring reasoning, honesty and independent judgment. J.O.S.I.E.-2 brings that research to open 2B, 4B and 9B models trained on Apple Silicon, with quantized releases for local inference.

Read the J.O.S.I.E.-2 research note ↗
